X-ZONE Instagram Concepts
Concept set // Reclaim Co for X-ZONE New Zealand

Six Instagram posts and a Reel for X-ZONE

Mocked at 1:1 feed size (1080 x 1080) in the approved social style: green #0D441F, lime #E0E64A and white, with navy only on the Joints piece. No red or orange, and never two dark-green tiles side by side. Every headline is a hook, in the voice of "Why we swapped the office for the Waitākere Ranges". Copy below each post is a suggested caption. The Reel with its shot list is at the bottom.

Content mix: five of the seven pieces teach (the herbs, how to apply a rub, bruise colours, a rolled ankle, the film), one is customer proof and one is the founders' story. Price appears once, as a footnote inside an educational post. That keeps the set inside an 80/20 educational-to-promotional balance.

Draft for client review
What the @xzonenz grid looks like today

No through-line from one tile to the next

  • Five or more palettes in nine tiles: maroon testimonial card, rainbow graphic, lime script on the challenge series, a red and yellow sale tile, bush photography.
  • Four typefaces in view at once, including a script face and an outlined display face that appear nowhere on the website or packaging.
  • The yellow koru mark, the strongest brand asset, is missing from most tiles.
  • The good material is there: founders in the bush, the "Tupākihi the bone mender" ingredient story, the lab result. It just isn't dressed consistently.
The rules this set follows

One system, repeated until it's recognisable

  • Green, lime and white grounds, mixed so the grid stays light. No two dark-green tiles sit side by side. Photos stay clear, with a green gradient only at the foot where the type sits.
  • One type family: Galano Grotesque in the brand's design files, Poppins in Canva and on the web, for headlines, labels and body alike.
  • Lime is the single accent, used as a highlighter on the phrase that matters. No red or orange on social. Navy appears only on Joints pieces.
  • Every headline is a hook. Logo in a white pill on photos, range pill top-right, reviews in the photo-on-top, colour-band-below layout. Same positions every time, so the template is reusable in Canva.

What is your bruise telling you?

The colour is a clock

Day 1 to 2Red to purple. Blood under the skin. Cool it, then Relief Rub.Day 3 to 6Blue to green. The body is breaking it down. Keep rubbing it in.Day 7 plusYellow to brown. Nearly done. Still sore? Have it checked.
Made in NZ
298 likes
xzone.nz A bruise changes colour for a reason. Red and purple is fresh blood under the skin. Blue and green means your body has started breaking it down. Yellow and brown is the clean-up crew finishing the job. What helps: cool it in the first hour, keep the area moving gently, and rub Relief Rub in twice a day. Kōwhai and harakeke were used for bruising long before we put them in a jar. If a bruise is still dark and painful after two weeks, or you bruise without knocking anything, see your GP. #XZoneRelief #BruiseCare #NaturalPainRelief #NZNativeHerbs #FirstAidTips #MadeInNZ

Our story

Why we swapped the office for the Waitākere Ranges

Jess and Dan on the racehorse rub that became eleven native herbs

Made in NZ
412 likes
xzone.nz We have been friends since we met at primary school in West Auckland, aged six. The Waitākere Ranges were on our doorstep the whole time, and so was a respect for what grows there. After years in corporate jobs, we bought a small business from a horse trainer who had made a rub for her race horses' sore muscles. Friends kept asking for "that horse stuff", so she made one for people. We did a rongoā course, did our research, and reformulated it, from two native herbs (harakeke and kūmarahou) to the eleven across our three ranges today. Two friends, one bush, and a jar that works. Read the full story at the link in bio. #XZoneNZ #MeetTheMakers #SmallBusinessNZ #WaitakereRanges #MadeInNZ #Rongoa

Reel // Nowhere else on earth // Educate

A silent 39-second film, rendered and delivered as an MP4 alongside this page. One continuous camera move per shot, long dissolves, no hard cuts, no voice, no music. Film grain, a soft vignette and letterbox bars hold it together. Every photograph is the client's own, from xzone.nz. Words are sparse and drift with the image.

Sound: delivered silent. Most Reels are watched muted, and the piece is written so the words do the work. If the client wants a bed, a licensed ambient track can be laid under it in the edit without changing a frame.

Why this one: it looks like nothing else in their grid or their competitors'. Slow, confident, and built entirely from photographs they already own, so the next one costs a half-day in the bush with a phone and a gimbal, not a studio.
